issue.title: flag_mutex_test.go: ineffective error-string assertion masks wrong error message
issue.body:
Found while reviewing #2386.

**Bug in test harness (flag_mutex_test.go:107):** the assertion checking the error string uses `t.Logf` instead of `t.Errorf`/`require.Contains`:

```go
if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), test.errStr) {
    t.Logf("Invalid error string %v", err)
}
```

So a wrong error message never fails the test. This is currently masking a real discrepancy: the `"set both flags"` case passes `--i 11 --ai 12` and expects `"option i cannot be set along with option ai"`, but the actual error is `"option i cannot be set along with option t"`. `MutuallyExclusiveFlags.check` uses `f.Names()[0]`, which returns the primary name (`t`), not the alias used on the CLI (`ai`).

**Fix:** change the assertion to `t.Errorf` (or `assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), test.errStr)`) so wrong messages fail, and decide whether the message should reference the flag name as typed on the command line (alias `ai`) rather than the primary name.

**Test coverage gap (related):** the regression test added in #2386 (`--i --q`) only covers "first member of group 0 × second member of group 1". The mirror cases — second member of group 0 (`--s --q`), and the issue-reproduction layout where the conflicting flag is the second member of both groups — are untested. Recommend adding at least one such case to pin the cross-group fix.
